prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The parent's density-weight relaxations all act on the *global* density weight scalar, but the TNS cost comes from *localized* congestion where a few bins stay overfull long after the global overflow has settled; instead of touching the density weight, tighten the wirelength-model gamma schedule so that in the late stage (when overflow is already low) the HPWL model becomes more accurate (smaller gamma), which shortens critical nets without adding congestion — but clamp the gamma floor to avoid the "cells pile up" regime that hurt c014/c018.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.516 robust(mean-std)=+0.095 min_case=+0.068 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.198 dWNS=+14.0% dTNS=+23.7% overflow~110
  bp-ng45: score=+0.250 dWNS=+26.1% dTNS=+24.3% overflow~136
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.068 dWNS=+5.6% dTNS=+7.7% overflow~125
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: all three cases improved, with no invalid runs. Gains concentrate in TNS (bp-ng45 +24.3%, ariane133 +23.7%) alongside WNS, consistent with a tighter late-stage gamma shortening critical nets without raising overflow (~110–136). bp_fe-ng45 moved least (+7.7% TNS), suggesting the gamma floor may be binding there or congestion already limits it. Next step: sweep the gamma floor per case (especially bp_fe-ng45) to confirm the clamp isn't leaving gains on the table while still avoiding the c014/c018 pile-up regime.
